newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares end higher on New York, Volvo jumps.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares end higher on New York, Volvo jumps.

text.p: Swedish shares ended higher on Monday, boosted by New York's Friday advance and its stronger Monday opening.
The Stockholm general index rose 1.74 percent to 2,734.49 in turnover of 4.51 billion crowns.
Cyclical shares benefited from speculation about stronger economic trends. The forestry sector rose 2.88 percent with MoDo rising 11.5 to 246.5.
Car maker Volvo jumped 10 crowns to 212 on hopes about the economy picking up, portfolio adjustments ahead of the share redemption, strong sales and a stronger dollar.

"The rise in Volvo is probably because foreigners who would like to sell their redemption rights for tax reasons are buying Volvo shares instead in order to retain the Volvo weight in their portfolios," one broker said.
Trade in investment company Incentive was halted before it announced it would merge its Gambro unit with Vivra's Renal Care business in a $1.59 billion deal.
Construction company Skanska closed up 8.5 crowns to 346 after announcing it would redeem one in every 10 shares at 400 crowns each.
